evidence.quote: The Xero API does not support basic API Key authentication.
The first step is to sign up for a free Xero account.
The quickest way to try out the API is to set up your demo company and dive into the API Explorer.
An MCP server that integrates with the MCP protocol
OAuth 1.0a is in the process of being deprecated and OAuth 2.0 is required for all new integrations.

result.notes: Xero's public Accounting/Payroll REST APIs use OAuth2 only (no API-key/basic auth). Any developer can sign up for a free Xero account, register an app in the developer portal to get a Client ID/Secret immediately, and build/test freely against a free demo company via the API Explorer — no paywall or approval needed to start developing. Publishing an app for broad public/production use (beyond the developer's own demo/trial orgs) goes through Xero's App Store review, and a premium 'Custom Connections' feature (client_credentials grant, no user consent screen) is a paid add-on — but base API access and OAuth2 authorization-code development is self-serve free. apis.guru lists 224 accounting-API endpoints (medium breadth). Xero publishes an official MCP server (@xeroapi/xero-mcp-server, MIT licensed, under the XeroAPI GitHub org) that runs locally via OAuth2 Custom Connections credentials.
result.one_liner: Xero is cloud accounting/bookkeeping software (invoicing, payroll, bank reconciliation) with a REST API for building financial integrations.
